title: USB-C UART Debug Adapter
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.where_the_quotations_are: Every one of them is in this file: fixed_requirements[].brief_evidence and brief_spec_rows[].brief_evidence. The count above is the sum of those two lists, so it is recomputable from this repository alone - re-read BRIEF.md and check each string is a substring of it. brief_spec_rows carries the quotations behind the README's spec table, which would otherwise cite the brief with the evidence left in a build script.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

open_decisions.decision: Which USB-UART bridge device to use.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires only that the bridge be "commonly available" and names no manufacturer, part number or family.

open_decisions.decision: The bridge's package, and how its land pattern, thermal pad (if any) and assembly process are handled.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no package. "small QFN" appears only in the benchmark header block and in metadata as a stressor, never in the design brief's requirements, so whether the chosen bridge is a QFN at all is a design outcome.

open_decisions.decision: Which USB-C receptacle to use — pin count, SMT versus through-hole, vertical/horizontal/mid-mount, retention scheme.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says "USB-C" and nothing about the receptacle variant or mounting style.

open_decisions.decision: The concrete implementation of the device-side CC network: what termination the USB Type-C specification requires for a device of this kind, on which pins, at what value and tolerance, and how both cable orientations are handled.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief demands a "correct" CC network but states no values, tolerances or topology; correctness is defined by the USB Type-C specification, which the design must cite rather than assume.

open_decisions.decision: The ESD protection strategy: discrete devices versus an array, which nets are protected (D+/D-, VBUS, CC, target-side signals), and the target ESD immunity level.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "USB ESD protection close to the connector" but names no device, no protected-net list beyond USB, and no immunity level or test standard.

open_decisions.decision: How the 3.3 V rail and the 3V3 reference pin are generated — bridge internal regulator, external regulator, or otherwise.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes 3.3 V as the UART level and requires a 3V3 reference pin, but is silent on where that rail comes from.

open_decisions.decision: Whether the 3V3 pin may source current to the target, and if so what current limit, protection or fusing applies.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief calls it a "3V3 reference" without specifying whether it is an output rail, and states no current budget.

open_decisions.decision: The VBUS input budget, the current level (if any) advertised to the source, and whether input protection (fuse, current limit, reverse protection, bulk capacitance) is included.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says only "bus-powered" and specifies no current draw, protection or advertised current level.

open_decisions.decision: The target header pinout, pin order, pin count and — if the compact locking option is taken — which connector family and pitch.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes the mandatory signal set and offers two header styles but does not choose between them, fix a pin order, or name a connector.

open_decisions.decision: Whether RTS/CTS is provided at all and, if it is, how its optionality is expressed: always-populated extra pins, do-not-populate parts, jumpers, or a build variant.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief marks RTS/CTS optional without requiring it or saying what optionality means mechanically or electrically.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting holes, and whether the board is a bare dongle, an inline adapter or an enclosed unit.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on mechanical form beyond requiring that the two connectors be clearly separated.

open_decisions.decision: How much separation between the USB and target-side connectors counts as "clearly separated", and how that is justified.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states the requirement qualitatively and gives no distance, keepout or creepage figure.

open_decisions.decision: Whether to actually use two layers or depart from that preference, and the full stackup: copper weight, dielectric thickness, dielectric constant, finish.
open_decisions.why_open: "Prefer two layers" is a preference, and the brief gives no stackup parameters; metadata's layer count is a likelihood, not a mandate.

open_decisions.decision: The differential impedance target for D+/D-, the method used to approximate it on the chosen stackup, and the trace geometry that follows.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires a documented impedance approximation but states no target value, tolerance, or calculation method.

open_decisions.decision: The grounding strategy on whatever stackup is chosen — how continuous a reference the differential pair gets, and how that is traded against routing the rest of the board.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on planes or return-path strategy; it follows only indirectly from the layer preference and the differential-pair requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Whether to include status/activity indication, additional broken-out control lines (for example a reset or bootloader line), test points, or bridge configuration such as descriptors and stored settings.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief mentions none of these; adding them is allowed as design freedom but must not be presented as a user requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Fabricator and assembly process selection, and the capability limits (minimum trace/space, drill, annular ring, single- versus double-sided assembly) the layout must respect.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no fabricator, process or capability set; "commonly available" constrains the bridge, not the process.
